offer_letter.markdown:
# Offer of employment — Head of Islamic Banking (Principal)

## 1. Job Offer

Dear {{employee.full_name}},

We are pleased to offer you the role of Head of Islamic Banking (Principal) at Absa Group. You will lead the Islamic Business Banking strategy, grow the business and customer base, drive Shari'ah-compliant banking solutions, lead product innovation, strengthen stakeholder relationships, manage Shari'ah governance and risk, and build a strong Islamic Banking team.

## 2. Start Date and Place of Work

Your employment starts on 1 December 2026. This is a permanent position. You will work at our Sandton head office. The first 3 months will be a probation period, during which we will support and assess your performance.

## 3. Hours and Pay

Your work hours are 40 hours a week, 8 hours a day, Monday to Friday from 08:00 to 17:00. You will get a 60-minute meal break after no more than 5 hours of work. Your basic salary is R18,000.00 per month, paid on the 25th of each month by EFT. We will deduct PAYE and 1% UIF from your pay, as required by law.

## 4. Leave

You will get 15 working days of paid annual leave each year. You will also get sick leave, family responsibility leave, maternity leave and parental leave as set out in your contract.

## 5. Next Steps

Please bring your ID and qualifications when you accept this offer. This offer expires on 30 November 2026. If you have questions, contact us at hr@example.co.za.

## 6. Acceptance

I, {{employee.full_name}}, accept this offer on {{date_signed}}.

contract.markdown:
# Contract of employment — Head of Islamic Banking (Principal)

## 1. Parties

This contract of employment is entered into between Absa Group, of 1 Main Road, Sandton (the Employer), and {{employee.full_name}}, identity number {{employee.id_number}}, of {{employee.address}} (the Employee).

## 2. Position and duties

The Employer appoints the Employee as Head of Islamic Banking (Principal). The Employee's duties include: Define and execute the Islamic Business Banking strategy.; Grow the business, customer base and market proposition.; Drive commercially sustainable Shari’ah-compliant banking solutions.; Lead product and proposition innovation.; Strengthen customer and stakeholder relationships.; Navigate Shari’ah governance, risk, regulatory and control requirements.; Partner across Product, Distribution, Operations, Risk, Compliance, Finance and Digital.; Build and lead a high-performing Islamic Banking capability.. The Employer may reasonably require the Employee to perform other duties consistent with the position.

## 3. Commencement

Employment commences on 1 December 2026 on a permanent basis.

## 4. Probation

The first 3 month(s) of employment are a probationary period during which the Employer will assess the Employee's performance against the requirements of the position and give reasonable evaluation, instruction, training, guidance or counselling where needed. Confirmation, extension or termination at the end of probation will follow a fair procedure.

## 5. Place of work

The Employee's place of work is Sandton, head office.

## 6. Hours of work

The Employee's ordinary hours of work are 40 hours per week, 8 hours per day over 5 days per week (Mon–Fri 08:00–17:00). A meal interval of 60 minutes is taken after no more than five hours of continuous work. The Employee is entitled to a daily rest period of at least 12 consecutive hours and a weekly rest period of at least 36 consecutive hours.

## 7. Remuneration

The Employee will be paid R18,000.00 per month (basic salary), equivalent to R103.85 per ordinary hour, payable monthly on the 25th by EFT. No other cash payments are payable. No payments in kind are made.

## 8. Overtime

Overtime is worked only by agreement and may not exceed ten hours in any week. Overtime is paid at 1.5 times the Employee's ordinary hourly wage, or, by agreement, compensated with paid time off. Work on a Sunday is paid at double the ordinary wage (or one and a half times if the Employee ordinarily works on Sundays), and work on a public holiday at double the ordinary wage.

## 9. Deductions

The following deductions will be made from the Employee's remuneration: PAYE; UIF 1%. No other deduction will be made without the Employee's written agreement in respect of a specific debt, or as required by law, a court order or an arbitration award.

## 10. Leave

The Employee is entitled to 15 working days of paid annual leave per annual leave cycle of 12 months, to be taken at a time agreed with the Employer and not later than six months after the end of the cycle. Sick leave: 30 days' paid sick leave in every 36-month cycle (during the first six months, one day for every 26 days worked); a medical certificate may be required for absences of more than two consecutive days or on more than two occasions in eight weeks. Maternity leave: at least 4 consecutive months. Parental leave: 10 consecutive days. Adoption and commissioning parental leave as provided in the Act. Family responsibility leave: 3 days' paid leave per year once employed for longer than four months and for at least four days a week.

## 11. Termination and notice

Either party may terminate this contract on written notice of one week if the employee has been employed for six months or less; two weeks if employed for more than six months but not more than one year; four weeks if employed for more than one year. Notice may not be given during any period of leave. Nothing in this clause prevents the Employer from terminating employment summarily for a fair reason following a fair procedure, or the parties from agreeing to waive notice.

## 12. Bargaining council or sectoral determination

No bargaining council agreement or sectoral determination applies to the Employer's business.

## 13. Confidentiality

The Employee will not, during or after employment, disclose or use any confidential information of the Employer, its clients or suppliers, except as required to perform the Employee's duties or by law.

## 14. Other documents

No other documents form part of this contract.

## 15. General

This contract records the whole agreement between the parties on its subject; any amendment must be in writing and signed by both parties. Where any term is less favourable to the Employee than the Basic Conditions of Employment Act or an applicable sectoral determination or collective agreement, the more favourable provision applies. The Employer will keep these particulars for three years after termination and will explain them to the Employee on request.

## 16. Signatures

Signed at ____________ on {{date_signed}}.

For the Employer: {{employer.signatory}}  ____________________

The Employee: {{employee.full_name}}  ____________________

plain_language.explanation: This clause names the two parties to the contract: Absa Group, based at 1 Main Road, Sandton, as the employer, and you as the employee, identified by your ID number and address. It confirms who is bound by this agreement.

You are being appointed as Head of Islamic Banking (Principal), and the clause lists your main duties, including setting Islamic Banking strategy, growing the business, driving Shari'ah-compliant solutions, leading innovation, managing relationships and governance, partnering across departments, and building a team. Your employer can also reasonably ask you to do other related tasks.
Your job starts on 1 December 2026. Your employment is permanent, meaning it has no fixed end date.

Your first 3 months are a probation period where your employer will check how well you are doing the job. They will give you fair guidance and support during this time, and any decision to confirm, extend or end your employment at the end of probation must follow a fair process.
You will work at the Sandton head office.

You will work 40 hours a week, 8 hours a day, 5 days a week, from Monday to Friday, 08:00 to 17:00. You get a 60-minute meal break if you work more than 5 hours straight, plus at least 12 hours of rest each day and 36 hours of rest each week.

You will earn R18,000.00 per month as your basic salary, which works out to R103.85 per hour. You will be paid monthly on the 25th by EFT. You will not receive any other cash payments or payments in kind.

You can only work overtime if you agree to it, and it cannot exceed 10 hours a week. Overtime pay is 1.5 times your normal hourly rate, or you can agree to take paid time off instead. If you work on a Sunday, you get double pay (or 1.5 times if Sundays are part of your normal schedule), and public holiday work is paid at double your normal rate.

Your employer will deduct PAYE (income tax) and 1% UIF from your salary. No other money will be taken from your pay unless you agree in writing, or the law, a court, or an arbitration award requires it.

You get 15 working days of paid annual leave each year, which must be taken within 6 months after the leave year ends, at a time you agree with your employer. You get 30 days of paid sick leave every 3 years (with a slower buildup in your first 6 months), and your employer can ask for a doctor's note if you are off more than 2 days in a row or more than twice in 8 weeks. You are also entitled to at least 4 months of maternity leave, 10 days of parental leave, adoption leave as the law provides, and 3 days of family responsibility leave per year once you've worked more than 4 months and at least 4 days a week.

Either you or your employer can end the contract with written notice: 1 week if you've worked 6 months or less, 2 weeks if you've worked between 6 months and 1 year, and 4 weeks if you've worked more than 1 year. Notice cannot be given while you are on leave. Your employer can also dismiss you immediately for a serious reason, as long as a fair process is followed, or both parties can agree to skip the notice period.
No bargaining council agreement or sectoral determination covers your employer's business, so these do not apply to your employment.

You must not share or use confidential information belonging to your employer, its clients or suppliers, whether you are still employed or have left. The only exceptions are if you need the information to do your job, or if the law requires you to share it.
No other documents are part of this contract besides what is written here.

This contract is the complete agreement between you and your employer, and any changes must be written and signed by both of you. If any part of this contract gives you less than what the law or a relevant agreement requires, the better terms will apply instead. Your employer will keep your employment records for 3 years after you leave and will explain any part of this contract to you if you ask.
This clause is the signing block. Both the employer's signatory and you, the employee, must sign and date the contract to confirm your agreement.
